issues.message: Exponential backtracking (proven). Severity: CRITICAL, confidence: HIGH.
issues.hint: Attack: "__" x n . "!" Replayed on PCRE2 10.49: preg_match fails from length 15 (backtrack_limit 100000, JIT off). The risky part is: [~\-_\/&.+]|\w|%\d+|\s Hotspot offsets: 4-28 Unbounded quantifier detected. May cause backtracking on non-matching input. Consider making it possessive (*+) or using atomic groups (?>...). Overlapping alternation branches inside a quantifier. e.g. (a|a)* or (ab|a)*. This can lead to catastrophic backtracking. Suggested (verify behavior): Consider using possessive quantifiers or atomic groups to limit backtracking. Suggested (verify behavior): Make alternatives mutually exclusive or order longer alternatives first. Suggested (verify behavior): replace nested quantifiers like (a+)+ with atomic groups (?>a+) or possessive quantifiers a++. Test with adversarial inputs like repeated strings followed by a non-matching character.

issues.message: Nested quantifiers can cause catastrophic backtracking.
issues.hint: Consider atomic groups (?>...) or possessive quantifiers — verify the rewrite still matches everything you need.

issues.message: Alternation branches "[~\\-_\\/&.+]" and "\\w" have overlapping character sets, which may cause unnecessary backtracking.
issues.hint: Consider using atomic groups (?>...) to prevent backtracking. Do not reorder overlapping alternatives as it changes match semantics.
